name: Collision Course '98

date.source: The federation's own broadcast, taped for delayed airing and posted as ten linked parts to rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy, msg_ids aw5MXK7F164J/lS6-P3lvWIUJ/k48WDbYM5PQJ/oydBhGdaqeMJ/BNHnya8IWNgJ/uRvEQoor0xYJ/FHNw55kwstkJ/pgJYoxkOLz8J/YLesXLbWuqwJ/_OYqRh-aZCYJ, whose ring announcer states the pay-per-view was 'held on Sunday February 1'.

no_appearances_reason: not structurally parsed -- read cover to cover for the wing's own operational/title facts but not converted match-by-match; the wing's own 1997 PPV record (BorderWars '97) is already unminted, and this pass follows the same convention rather than mint a partial roster off one show.
notes: The federation's own final full pay-per-view before its closure the following month. Crowns four new champions: the World Heavyweight title (Gary Albright defeats the previously-undefeated champion Scimitar), the National title ("Ice Cold" Joe Williams defeats "Mr Pain" Jack Michaels), the World Television title (The Gorilla defeats "Too Cool" Chris Hopper with an assist from a rival stable), and the first-ever Random Tagteam title (Mexx and The Psychotic Doctor). Also unifies the National and World tag titles under one set of belts (Jacob Skar and Don Ford defeat Jack Strange and Phoenix Huston) and crowns a new Light-Heavyweight champion from a previously vacant title (Jinsei Shakanuzi defeats Vampyro).
